pr_title: drivers: uart_imx: Fix the poll_in function
pr_body:
Current poll_in function implementation blocks when there is no data available. The Zephyr documentation for poll_in expects the function to return -1 when no data is available.

Fixes #45533

issue_context.title: uart_imx_poll_in() seems to be a blocking function
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**

As per #45468, I'm filling a bug report against the UART driver for NXP i.MX7.  The function `uart_imx_poll_in()` seems to be a blocking call, as [wrongly documented in our doc](https://docs.zephyrproject.org/latest/hardware/peripherals/uart.html).  The function, instead, should be non-blocking and must return `-1` when there is no valid data.

**Expected behavior**
Non blocking and return `-1` when no valid data is available.

**Impact**
Different behavior compare to other UART drivers.

**Additional context**
https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/45468#issuecomment-1122620593

review_comments: Could we use the `-EIO` (`-5`) instead of `-EPERM` (`-1`)?

The document for the `uart_poll_in `function found at https://docs.zephyrproject.org/latest/hardware/peripherals/uart.html states:
`-1 – If no character was available to read (i.e. the UART input buffer was empty).`
Can you add a separate issue against the API if this is something we wish to change for the UART poll API.
Sorry, I didn't look into the UART header. Not sure how `-1` got in there, normally `-<ERRNO>` is used from `errno.h`.
Please do add an issue and if possible a PR if this is something that needs to be addressed.
